- **Licences:** none recorded
- **Pay:** B16 USD 40918–61130 annual, effective 2026-07-01

## EMST role: Wildlife biologist (state variant, entry level; P2)

*Match:* `skos:broadMatch`, confidence 0.5, unreviewed agent draft (`emst-x5-tx:R15-wildlife-biologist/state:2682`). *Authority position (editorial):* resource-manager.

**Competency targets at this level (agent draft)**

- Capture, handle and mark wildlife and fish humanely and safely — entry L1
- Assess species habitat requirements and habitat condition — entry L1 *(distinguishing)*
- Detect and record wildlife by direct observation, sign and standardized surveys — entry L1
- Assess effects on protected species and conduct interagency consultation on proposed actions — entry L1
- Identify organisms from field characters, specimens, images and recordings — entry L1
- Use AI tools responsibly in everyday environmental work — entry L1
- Validate AI-generated work products before professional use — entry L1
- Navigate and travel safely in remote terrain with and without digital aids — entry L1
- Assess and monitor biodiversity across species and habitats — entry L1
- Analyze environmental data statistically and interpret the results — entry L1

**Main tasks at this level (indicative % of time, agent draft)**

- Capture animals with traps, nets or electrofishing following the approved animal-care protocol and permit conditions — 8.2% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Immobilize an animal chemically where authorized, monitoring vital signs until recovery and recording drug doses — 7.2% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Deploy camera traps and acoustic recorders at survey stations to the protocol's height, orientation and settings, recording station metadata — 7.2% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Conduct ground or aerial counts of target species along defined survey units to support abundance estimation — 7.2% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Measure habitat attributes such as cover, structure, water and forage at used and available sites following a habitat-use study protocol — 7.2% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Mark captured animals with tags or other marks while recording biological data within protocol handling-time and stress limits — 5.7% *(needed at entry)*
- Apply zoonotic disease and personal safety precautions when handling wildlife, including protective equipment and decontamination — 5.7% *(needed at entry)*
- Conduct point-count, transect or call-playback wildlife surveys to protocol, recording detections, distance bands and survey conditions — 5.7% *(needed at entry)*
- Observe animal movement, foraging and breeding behaviour at study sites, recording behaviour and habitat context on standardized forms — 5.7% *(needed at entry)*
- Identify regional plants and animals to species with dichotomous keys and diagnostic features, collecting evidence for any record not identified with certainty — 5.7% *(needed at entry)*
- Verify species records submitted by crews or volunteers against attached photos, recordings or vouchers before they enter the program database — 5.7% *(needed at entry)*
- Compile species and habitat occurrence information for an action area, documenting the sources and survey dates used for each listed species — 5.7% *(needed at entry)*

## EMST role: Fisheries and aquatic biologist (state variant, entry level; P2)

*Match:* `skos:broadMatch`, confidence 0.55, unreviewed agent draft (`emst-x5-tx:R16-fisheries-aquatic-biologist/state:2682`). *Authority position (editorial):* resource-manager.

**Competency targets at this level (agent draft)**

- Manage fish populations and habitats to stated conservation and harvest objectives — entry L1 *(distinguishing)*
- Apply field biosecurity and decontamination protocols — entry L1
- Operate small boats and work safely on water in aquatic, coastal and marine field settings — entry L1
- Capture, handle and mark wildlife and fish humanely and safely — entry L1
- Measure water quality and survey aquatic communities in the field — entry L1
- Use AI tools responsibly in everyday environmental work — entry L1
- Validate AI-generated work products before professional use — entry L1
- Collect trace-level and genetic environmental samples without contamination — entry L1
- Operate fish hatchery and aquatic propagation programmes — entry L1
- Analyze environmental data statistically and interpret the results — entry L1

**Main tasks at this level (indicative % of time, agent draft)**

- Sample fish populations by electrofishing, netting or hydroacoustics following the survey protocol to estimate abundance and size structure — 9.3% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Capture animals with traps, nets or electrofishing following the approved animal-care protocol and permit conditions — 7.2% *(needed at entry)*
- Immobilize an animal chemically where authorized, monitoring vital signs until recovery and recording drug doses — 7.2% *(needed at entry)*
- Execute person-overboard, capsize and cold-water immersion procedures for a small-boat crew during drills and real events — 7.2% *(needed at entry)*
- Work sampling gear such as grabs, nets, sondes or traps over the side of a small vessel, keeping crew clear of lines and winches — 7.2% *(needed at entry)*
- Collect grab water samples at locations and depths that represent the condition of interest, recording flow and site conditions at collection — 7.2% *(needed at entry)*
- Screen field measurement results against applicable water-quality criteria before leaving the site, triggering resampling or notification when an exceedance appears — 7.2% *(needed at entry)*
- Adapt the decontamination procedure on site when a new pathogen or invasive organism is suspected, escalating the finding before moving on — 7.2% *(needed at entry)*
- Decontaminate boots, gear, boats and vehicles between field sites with the protocol's method and contact time for the target organisms — 7.2% *(needed at entry)*
- Mark captured animals with tags or other marks while recording biological data within protocol handling-time and stress limits — 5.5% *(needed at entry)*
- Sequence site visits from lower-risk to higher-risk waters or stands so that crews cannot carry organisms from infested to uninfested sites — 5.5% *(needed at entry)*
- Spawn broodstock following the genetic management plan's mating scheme, recording parentage for each lot — 5.5%

## EMST role: Water and wastewater treatment operator (state variant, entry level; P2)

*Match:* `skos:relatedMatch`, confidence 0.2, unreviewed agent draft (`emst-x5-tx:R25-water-wastewater-operator/state:2682`). *Authority position (editorial):* regulated-party.

**Competency targets at this level (agent draft)**

- Operate drinking water treatment processes to meet water quality targets — entry L1 *(distinguishing)*
- Operate wastewater treatment and resource-recovery processes to permit limits — entry L1
- Practice within licensure scope and responsible charge — entry L1
- Protect operational technology at environmental utilities and facilities — entry L1
- Manage field sample custody and field quality control — entry L1
- Apply safety practices and stop-work authority across field, facility and incident settings — entry L1
- Work safely on hazardous, industrial and energized field sites — entry L1
- Use AI tools responsibly in everyday environmental work — entry L1
- Validate AI-generated work products before professional use — entry L1
- Manage a municipal stormwater programme to meet permit conditions — entry L1

**Main tasks at this level (indicative % of time, agent draft)**

- Adjust coagulant dosing from jar test results when raw-water turbidity, temperature or organic content changes — 6.6% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Verify disinfection contact time against required inactivation values at each operating flow and correct shortfalls before water enters distribution — 6.1% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Adjust aeration and sludge wasting rates using solids inventory, settleability and dissolved-oxygen trends to hold effluent within permit limits — 6.1% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Diagnose a biological process upset from microscopic examination, foam, odor and settling behavior before laboratory results confirm it — 6.1% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Respond to a treatment upset by isolating the affected process unit, bringing backup treatment online and notifying the primacy agency — 4.8% *(needed at entry)*
- Route peak wet-weather flows through the plant to protect biological treatment, recording any bypass or overflow for required reporting — 4.8% *(needed at entry)*
- Operate anaerobic digestion and solids handling to meet biosolids pathogen-reduction and stability requirements while recovering digester gas — 4.8% *(needed at entry)*
- Monitor automated control loops and alarms on a treatment process, checking automated responses against field observations of process condition — 4.8% *(needed at entry)*
- Complete chain-of-custody records for every sample from collection to laboratory receipt, recording each transfer, seal and temperature check — 4.8% *(needed at entry)*
- Collect field duplicates, splits and blanks at the frequency the sampling plan specifies, labelling them so the laboratory cannot identify them — 4.8% *(needed at entry)*
- Identify signs of potential hazardous materials at a field site, such as drums, stained soil, odours or unusual debris, before disturbing them — 4.8% *(needed at entry)*
- Isolate an incidentally discovered hazardous material, establishing a safe distance and notifying the designated responder before any further work — 4.8% *(needed at entry)*

*Credential gates (issuer verified):* Drinking water treatment operator certification (Grades I-IV / Class A-D, state-specific) (required); Wastewater treatment operator certification (Grades I-IV) (required)
